title: Every Clock in the Machine Economy Strikes This Fall. We Lined Up the Dates.
excerpt: September 15 is a double-header: Cloudflare walls off mixed-use AI crawlers the same day the Senate votes cloture on the CLARITY Act. Two weeks later the fall conference corridor opens, and one day after TOKEN2049 ends, Bitcoin's widely watched 1,064/364-day cycle pattern projects its turning point. We lined up every verified date from now to the ERCOT audit in December — and put them on a calendar you can subscribe to.
description: The verified date math of fall 2026: the Sept 15 Cloudflare/CLARITY double-header, the KBW→TOKEN2049 conference corridor, Bitcoin's 1,064/364-day cycle window around Oct 9, the GENIUS docket close, and ERCOT's December audit.

lede: While pulling dates for our new [calendar page](/calendar), we noticed something: the machine economy's clocks are synchronized this fall, and nobody set them that way on purpose. **September 15** is a genuine double-header — Cloudflare starts default-blocking mixed-use AI crawlers the same day the Senate holds its make-or-break cloture vote on the CLARITY Act. Two weeks later the fall conference corridor opens in Seoul, runs through the world's largest crypto conference in Singapore — and ends one day before **October 9**, the projected turning point of the most-watched pattern in Bitcoin: 1,064 days up, 364 days down, repeating since 2015. We lined up every date we could verify.

sections.heading: The cluster, in order
paras: **August 19** (already behind us): President Trump hosted Ripple's Garlinghouse, Coinbase's Armstrong, ICE's Sprecher, Robinhood's Tenev, and Kraken's Sethi at the White House — SEC Chair Atkins in the room, one day after regulators unveiled new crypto rules — and publicly pressed Congress to pass the CLARITY Act. That set the stage for everything below.

**September 14**: Congress reconvenes with 14 working days before the October election recess. **September 15**: the double-header (next section). **September 29 – October 1**: Korea Blockchain Week in Seoul. **October 5–11**: TOKEN2049 Week in Singapore, with the main event October 7–8 — ~25,000 attendees, the biggest stage in crypto. **October 9**: the Bitcoin cycle pattern's projected turning point. **October 19**: Treasury's GENIUS Act stablecoin comment docket closes. Then the election recess swallows Washington — and on **December 10 and 17**, ERCOT's audit of ~300 proposed Texas data centers reports out, deciding how much of the machine economy's physical buildout is real.

sections.heading: September 15: the double-header
paras: Two unrelated institutions picked the same day. **Cloudflare** default-blocks crawlers that blend search, AI training, and agent use on ad-hosting pages — for new customers, new sites, and every free-plan site. The open web starts gating machine traffic at the edge, and paid, identified access becomes the sanctioned way in. That's the thesis behind pay-per-call rails like x402, implemented as a network default at one of the internet's biggest chokepoints.

Same day, the **Senate votes cloture on the CLARITY Act** — 60 votes to advance the digital-asset market-structure bill, and a failed vote likely kills it this Congress. One day decides both how machines get charged at the door of the web, and which agency writes the rulebook for the money they pay with. If you follow one date this fall, it's this one.

sections.heading: The conference corridor
paras: Announcements in this industry cluster around stages. **Korea Blockchain Week** (Seoul, September 29 – October 1) opens the corridor; **TOKEN2049 Singapore** (October 7–8, inside a week that runs October 5–11) closes it in front of 25,000 people from 160 countries. If an agent-payments platform, an x402 integration, or a major rail partnership is brewing — this is the fortnight it goes public. We'll be watching both from the rail-data side: announcement spikes show up in our collectors before they show up in press releases.

sections.heading: The Bitcoin metronome
paras: Now the pattern the operator of every crypto treasury already has circled. Since 2015, Bitcoin's cycle has repeated with eerie regularity: roughly **1,064 days of rise, then roughly 364 days of decline**. The 2015 low to the December 2017 high: ~1,064 days. That high to the December 2018 low: ~364. The 2018 low to the November 2021 high: ~1,064. That high to the November 2022 low: ~364. The 2022 low to the **October 6, 2025 all-time high (~$126K)**: ~1,064 again. Count 364 days forward from that peak and you land in the first week of October 2026 — analyses circulating this summer put the projected turning point around **October 9**. The world's largest crypto conference ends the day before.

Here's our honest read, because patterns deserve the same skepticism we give indexer dashboards: this is **three repetitions**, it's entangled with the four-year halving cycle it may simply be restating, and a sample of three proves a rhyme, not a law. But a pattern doesn't need to be causal to matter — it needs to be *believed*. Enough of the market has this date circled that the window itself becomes an event: positioning, headlines, and volatility cluster around it whether or not the math means anything. We're not telling you what Bitcoin will do (we're a data lab, not advisors, and this is not investment advice). We're telling you the machine economy's biggest funding source has a scheduled appointment with its own mythology — ten days before the stablecoin rulebook's comment docket closes.

stats.d: Days of rise in each cycle since 2015 — low to high, three times in a row.
Days of decline in each completed cycle — high to low, almost exactly a year.
Projected turning point, 364 days after the October 6, 2025 all-time high. Pattern, not prophecy.

sections.heading: Put it on your calendar — literally
paras: All of these dates — with sources, countdowns, and why-it-matters notes — live on our new [calendar page](/calendar), which we'll keep current the way we keep [Rail Pulse](/#rail-pulse) and [Texas Watch](/texas) current. You can [download the whole thing as an .ics file](/calendar/ics) and drop it into Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, or Outlook, or grab single events off the page. When a date moves — and in Washington, dates move — the page and the feed update the same day. We'll log what actually happens on each of them, same as we logged [x402's record week](/blog/x402-record-day-money-didnt-move) and [ERCOT's audit order](/blog/texas-ercot-300-data-center-audit).
